title: AlphaResearch: Accelerating New Algorithm Discovery with Language Models

mechanism.domainTask: open-ended algorithm discovery with research-proposal and program co-optimization
mechanism.populationDetail: An undivided trajectory and candidates pool stores many idea-program-result triplets; no islands or maintained tree are described.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The algorithm explicitly retains one best-so-far triplet (\(i_{\mathrm{best}}\), \(p_{\mathrm{best}}\), \(r_{\mathrm{best}}\)) when execution score improves.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Accepted triplets are appended to an effectively growing trajectory/candidates pool, while a separate best-so-far record uses elitist comparison.
mechanism.generationDetail: One sampled prior program \(p_t\) is edited through exact SEARCH/REPLACE patches conditioned on a newly generated idea; the idea track is separate meta-guidance, not a second program parent.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: The RM scalar gates idea continuation; execution verification/measurement scores are injected into future prompts when a trajectory state is sampled and stored with candidates.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: One sampled state supplies the true program parent plus idea/result context; no multi-parent fusion or tournament selection is specified.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Joint proposal-meta-guidance and targeted program editing with a separate learned peer-review reward model; current taxonomy does not fully represent this artifact/role split.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/AlphaResearch Accelerating New Algorithm Discovery with Language Models.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Survey currently places AlphaResearch under Large-Scale Modification, but Appendix B requires targeted SEARCH/REPLACE edits and forbids rewriting the entire program; review that placement. Multi-model subtype is intentionally unclear because AlphaResearch-RM-7B evaluates proposals rather than generating competing candidates.
